accepted.question_text: Riemann's hypothesis asks whether every nontrivial zero of the Riemann zeta function has real part 1/2; equivalently, whether all zeros other than the negative even integers are of the form s = 1/2 + iτ.

evidence.quote: This one is usually known as the Riemann hypothesis and is the most famous and important of the unsolved conjectures in mathematics.
The Riemann hypothesis now says that all other zeros are of the form s = 1/2 + iτ.

accepted.question_text: Classify the convex polytopes that admit a monohedral tiling of R^d, meaning a tiling of Euclidean space by congruent copies of a single convex polytope.

evidence.quote: For instance, the convex polytopes that can give a monohedral tiling of R^d have not yet been classified, even for the plane.

accepted.question_text: Determine exactly which polyominoes tile the whole plane.

evidence.quote: As another example of one of the problems that emerged, it is unknown at this time (2003) which polyominos tile the whole plane.

accepted.question_text: Determine the densest possible packing of congruent spheres in Euclidean space in arbitrary dimension.

evidence.quote: (18c) Densest packing of spheres. Still unsolved in general.
The Leech lattice is conjecturally the densest packing in 24 dimensions.

accepted.question_text: Extend uniformization by automorphic functions to higher complex dimensions and to the generalizations alluded to in the survey, where the source states that the higher-dimensional case remains largely open.

evidence.quote: For higher (complex) dimension things are still largely open and that also holds for a variety of generalizations, loc. cit. and [1, 14].

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 12. Extension of Kronecker's theorem on Abelian fields to any algebraic realm of rationality.

evidence.quote: Nowadays there is great interest in and great progress on 'non-Abelian class field theory' in the form of the conjectured Langlands correspondence.
The correspondence is also supposed to satisfy a number of strong extra properties.

needs_review.question_text_raw: Problem 15. Rigorous foundation of Schubert's enumerative calculus.

evidence.quote: In spite of a great deal of progress, see loc. cit., there remains much to be done to obtain a true enumerative geometry such as Schubert dreamt of.

needs_review.question_text_raw: The seven millennium problems were formulated by the Clay Institute and listed here without full technical statements.

evidence.quote: These seven are far more deeply imbedded in technically sophisticated mathematics (except one). They are: The Riemann hypothesis; Yang-Mills theory and the mass gap hypothesis; The P vs NP problem; The Navier-Stokes equations; The Poincare conjecture; The Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture; The Hodge conjecture.
